title: How seeds grow: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Inside a seed is a baby plant.
A seed needs water, air, and cold to grow.
The first part to come out of the seed is the leaf.
The root takes in water and nutrients.
The shoot grows downward into the soil.
The young plant uses sunlight to make food.

items.why: “Inside the seed is a baby plant.”

items.q: What is the first step called?
Which way does the root grow?
items.why: “The root grows downward into the soil.”

items.q: What does the root help the baby plant do?
items.why: “It helps the baby plant stay in place.”

items.q: What is the young plant called when it is above the ground?
items.why: “Now the seedling is above the ground.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: A seed has a baby plant inside it, and it needs water, air and warmth to grow. First the root grows down, and then the shoot grows up through the soil. The leaves open, and the plant uses sunlight to make food.

items.q: What does a seed need to grow?
items.model: It needs water, air and warmth.
It grows down into the soil. It holds the baby plant in place, and it takes in water and nutrients.

items.q: What can the young plant do when its first leaves open?
items.model: It can use sunlight to make food. This helps it grow stronger.

items.q: Have you ever planted a seed? What did you plant, and what happened?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the steps in the order of the text.
items: The seed gets water and wakes up
The root grows down into the soil
The shoot pushes up through the soil
The plant grows bigger and stronger
